Incorporating SLOOS insights tilts the assessment modestly more negative than the FSR-only read. Banks reported tighter standards and soft demand for C&I loans, citing the uncertain economic outlook, industry-specific problems, and lower risk tolerance; this suggests lingering headwinds for business credit even as the Fed maintains strong accommodation. Offsetting positives include large banks easing standards for several residential mortgage categories, small banks expecting stronger consumer loan demand, and signs that foreign banks saw firmer C&I demand—supportive for household credit and some cross-border business activity. Net: policy remains highly supportive, but bank lending dynamics to firms remain constrained, warranting a slightly more negative tone versus the prior -0.10.
